title: Change-Centric Management of Versions in an XML Warehouse
abstract: A structured-document precursor for cross-version lineage. The work stores evolving XML snapshots through completed deltas and persistent identifiers, allowing changes between successive versions to be represented without treating each document snapshot as unrelated.

title: Detecting Changes in XML Documents
abstract: Presents an XML differencing algorithm that matches nodes between old and new document versions and detects operations including subtree moves. Persistent identifiers and structural matching make it relevant to element correspondence across revisions, although the domain is structured XML rather than multimodal attachments.

title: X-Diff: an effective change detection algorithm for XML documents
abstract: Detects structural changes between versions of XML documents under an unordered-tree model. It is relevant as a transfer mechanism for structural element correspondence and semantic differencing across document revisions.

title: Change Detection In XML Documents
abstract: Uses top-down and bottom-up XML matching to identify insertions, deletions, updates, copies, and moves between document versions. The operation-level correspondence is useful precedent for revision lineage, while not addressing page regions or multimodal content directly.
venue: International Workshop on XML-Based Data Management

title: Schema-less, semantics-based change detection for XML documents
abstract: Associates XML elements across successive versions without requiring a schema and uses semantics to preserve identifiers through substantial structural change. It is particularly relevant to stable element identity when revisions alter document organization.

title: Temporal queries and version management in XML-based document archives
abstract: Studies storage and querying of multi-version XML document histories, including queries over document content and its evolution. It provides transfer evidence for version-aware element histories but does not cover spatial document regions or multimodal attachments.

title: Temporal and multi-versioned XML documents: A survey
abstract: Surveys temporal and multi-version XML research, including change detection, version storage, and querying of evolving document elements. It is useful background for separating snapshot identity, change representation, and persistent element history.

title: Bridging the gap between tracking and detecting changes in XML
abstract: Connects explicit change tracking with post-hoc differencing so that higher-level document changes can be represented rather than only low-level text edits. This is relevant to revision semantics and element lineage, though it operates on XML rather than rendered multimodal documents.

title: The Rationale of PROV
abstract: Explains the design rationale of the W3C PROV model, in which entities, activities, agents, and derivation relations describe how artifacts came to be. This is transfer evidence for representing version and evidence lineage, but it does not prescribe page-, region-, cell-, or span-level document grounding.

title: The Open Provenance Model core specification (v1.1)
abstract: Defines a graph-based provenance representation intended to exchange causal histories across systems. Its entity and process relationships are a transferable substrate for hierarchical version lineage, but spatial document coordinates are outside its scope.

title: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance
abstract: Introduces distinct notions of why-provenance and where-provenance for database query results, formalizing both justification and source location. This is transfer evidence for exact source attribution, not direct evidence for multimodal documents or revised attachments.

title: Tracing the lineage of view data in a warehousing environment
abstract: Defines lineage for derived warehouse data and develops methods for tracing an output item back to the source items that contributed to it. The fine-grained source-to-result relationship is transferable to evidence provenance but does not itself model document regions or versions.

title: Provenance Semirings
abstract: Provides an algebraic framework that annotates data with provenance and propagates those annotations through queries. It is foundational transfer work for compositional evidence lineage, but its identifiers refer to database data rather than document pages, cells, regions, or answer spans.

title: Demonstration of ProvSQL Update Provenance through Temporal Databases
abstract: Demonstrates provenance for database INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations together with temporal history and time-travel behavior. It is transfer evidence for provenance across revisions, rather than direct validation of document or workbook element lineage.

title: CiteVQA: Benchmarking Evidence Attribution for Trustworthy Document Intelligence
abstract: Benchmarks document question answering in which a system must provide an answer together with element-level bounding-box citations to the supporting source regions. It directly evaluates answer attribution inside document pages, but does not add cross-version attachment lineage.

title: DocAttriBench: Benchmarking Answer Grounding in Document Visual Question Answering
abstract: Benchmarks document VQA answer attribution at the level of document elements, including text blocks, tables, and images. It evaluates both answer correctness and whether the predicted answer is grounded in the correct supporting element.

title: BBox DocVQA: A Large Scale Bounding Box Grounded Dataset for Enhancing Reasoning in Document Visual Question Answer
abstract: Extends document VQA with bounding-box grounding so that supporting regions are explicitly associated with answers. The dataset includes single- and multi-region as well as single- and multi-page evidence cases, making it directly relevant to region-level provenance.

title: DocScope: Benchmarking Verifiable Reasoning for Trustworthy Long-Document Understanding
abstract: Represents verifiable long-document reasoning through a structured trajectory containing evidence pages, supporting evidence regions, factual statements, and a final answer. This directly exercises a page-to-region-to-claim-to-answer hierarchy, although attachment-version identity is not part of the representation.

title: HierDoc: Hierarchical Page-to-Region Evidence Routing for Long-Document Visual Question Answering
abstract: Uses hierarchical evidence routing that first identifies relevant pages and then selects supporting semantic regions within those pages. Region representations can include crops, OCR text, and table content, making the work directly relevant to hierarchical document evidence localization.

title: Towards Self-Explainable Document Visual Question Answering with Chain-of-Explanation Predictions
abstract: Introduces document VQA reasoning that explicitly identifies relevant evidence and localizes an answer region before producing the answer. The approach is pertinent to making document answers auditable at source-region level.

title: Spatially Grounded Explanations in Vision Language Models for Document Visual Question Answering
abstract: Grounds explanatory rationales for document VQA in spatial subregions of the source document and constrains answering to selected evidence areas. It directly connects language reasoning with localized page evidence.

title: ARIAL: An Agentic Framework for Document VQA with Precise Answer Localization
abstract: Combines document question answering with explicit spatial answer localization through text-to-region alignment. It evaluates both textual answers and localization, directly addressing the need to preserve precise source coordinates alongside an answer.

title: BoundingDocs: a Unified Dataset for Document Question Answering with Spatial Annotations
abstract: Associates document question-answer pairs with bounding boxes indicating the exact position of relevant source content. The spatial annotations make it useful for evaluating region-level provenance, while version lineage and workbook cells remain outside its scope.

title: MAGE-RAG: Multigranular Adaptive Graph Evidence for Agentic Multimodal RAG in Long-Document QA
abstract: Models long documents as an evidence graph containing page- and element-level nodes with relationships such as containment, reading order, layout adjacency, and section hierarchy. Unlike page-only retrieval, it exposes finer-grained document elements for evidence selection, though it does not address cross-version lineage.

title: From Rows to Reasoning: A Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Framework for Spreadsheet Understanding
abstract: Targets enterprise spreadsheets with multiple linked sheets and multimodal content such as embedded images. It builds retrieval units at multiple spreadsheet granularities, providing direct evidence for workbook-level multimodal understanding but not comprehensive revision provenance.

title: SpreadsheetLLM: Encoding Spreadsheets for Large Language Models
abstract: Develops spreadsheet-specific encodings that preserve cell addresses, values, formats, and structural relationships while compressing large sheets for language models. It advances spreadsheet structure understanding but does not establish cell lineage across workbook revisions.

title: SpreadsheetBench: Towards Challenging Real World Spreadsheet Manipulation
abstract: Benchmarks manipulation of real-world spreadsheets containing multiple sheets, multiple tables, non-standard relationships, and non-textual elements. It is useful for assessing workbook complexity beyond isolated clean tables, although provenance across versions is not a benchmark target.

title: Back to the Future: A workbook time machine for spread sheet creation benchmarks
abstract: Constructs spreadsheet creation tasks by rewinding completed workbooks into earlier states, yielding trajectories that can include formulas, charts, pivot tables, and conditional formatting. The explicit before-and-after workbook states are relevant to revision research, though the work does not itself define persistent semantic cell lineage.

title: SheetCopilot: Bringing Software Productivity to the Next Level through Large Language Models
abstract: Uses language-model planning and spreadsheet operations to execute natural-language tasks over spreadsheets. Its benchmark and stateful manipulation framework provide evidence about spreadsheet interaction and structure, but not stable provenance across workbook revisions.

title: InstructExcel: A Benchmark for Natural Language Instruction in Excel
abstract: Benchmarks natural-language-driven Excel editing over a broad set of spreadsheet operations and real spreadsheet files. It provides evidence for workbook manipulation capabilities, but it is not a provenance or cross-version cell-lineage benchmark.

title: Large Language Models for Spreadsheets: Benchmarking Progress and Evaluating Performance with FLARE
abstract: Evaluates language models on spreadsheet reasoning tasks that include formula logic and auditing-oriented capabilities. It is useful for characterizing workbook reasoning gaps, but does not validate comprehensive versioned cell provenance.

title: Robust Table Detection and Structure Recognition from Heterogeneous Document Images
abstract: Performs table detection and structural reconstruction on heterogeneous document images, including difficult structures involving spanning cells and blank areas. The explicit recovery of cell topology is relevant to preserving source-cell semantics before downstream grounding.

title: Split, Embed and Merge: An accurate table structure recognizer
abstract: Recognizes complex table structures by first predicting fine-grained grids and then merging them into logical cells, using both visual and textual information. This is directly relevant to recovering spanning and merged-cell structure needed for precise cell grounding.

title: Table Structure Recognition and Form Parsing by End-to-End Object Detection and Relation Parsing
abstract: Jointly detects table or form components and predicts structural relations among cells and other elements. The relation-based representation is relevant to retaining logical table structure rather than reducing a document to unstructured OCR text.

title: A large-scale dataset for end-to-end table recognition in the wild
abstract: Provides document-table annotations that include table-body location, cell spatial position, logical row and column coordinates, text, and row or column spanning information. These annotations directly support evaluation of structural preservation needed for later cell-level provenance.

title: A Prototype Document Image Analysis System for Technical Journals
abstract: An early document-image analysis system that combines page segmentation and structural parsing for technical journal pages. It demonstrates that preservation of page organization and document structure was an explicit document-analysis problem well before modern multimodal models.

title: High Performance Document Layout Analysis
abstract: Develops robust geometric and statistical methods for document page layout analysis. It is foundational evidence for segmenting heterogeneous pages into meaningful regions before reading-order reconstruction or region-level evidence grounding.
venue: Symposium on Document Image Understanding Technology

title: A machine-learning approach for analyzing document layout structures with two reading orders
abstract: Analyzes document layout while explicitly modeling pages that use different reading-order conventions, including horizontal and vertical text organization. It is relevant to preserving relationships among text lines and regions in complex scanned documents.

title: Abstract argumentation for reading order detection
abstract: Models reading-order decisions among document-page components using an abstract-argumentation formulation. The work directly concerns reconstruction of semantic ordering relationships between detected regions rather than region detection alone.

title: XYLayoutLM: Towards Layout-Aware Multimodal Networks For Visually-Rich Document Understanding
abstract: A layout-aware multimodal document model that explicitly addresses reading order and two-dimensional page structure in visually rich documents. Its treatment of ordered layout elements is relevant to preserving semantic document structure for later grounding.

title: Reading order detection in visually-rich documents with multi-modal layout-aware relation prediction
abstract: Predicts reading-order relations using visual, semantic, and positional information from document elements. It directly evaluates ordering relationships in complex visually rich layouts, supporting structural preservation beyond independent region detection.

title: Rethinking Reading Order: Toward Generalizable Document Understanding with LLM-based Relation Modeling
abstract: Uses language-model-based relation modeling to infer global reading order and inter-element layout relationships. The work is relevant to hierarchical document structure because it models dependencies between elements rather than treating OCR blocks independently.

title: Resolving References in Visually-Grounded Dialogue via Text Generation
abstract: Transfer-domain work on resolving conversational references to visual entities. It generates descriptions of intended referents and uses vision-language grounding to resolve them, offering a mechanism potentially portable to message-to-attachment references but no workplace-document validation.

title: The PhotoBook Dataset: Building Common Ground through Visually-Grounded Dialogue
abstract: Introduces visually grounded dialogues in which participants repeatedly refer to images while building common ground, enabling study of reference chains over conversational context. This is transfer evidence for cross-modal reference resolution rather than document-attachment grounding.

title: Refer, Reuse, Reduce: Generating Subsequent References in Visual and Conversational Contexts
abstract: Studies how referring expressions evolve as visual entities are mentioned repeatedly in dialogue and models generation using both conversational and visual context. The resulting reference mechanisms are transferable to attachment references but are evaluated on image dialogue rather than workplace documents.

title: Phrase Grounding by Soft-Label Chain Conditional Random Field
abstract: Transfer-domain phrase grounding that maps textual entity mentions to image regions while modeling dependencies among multiple mentions. It supplies a region-localization mechanism but does not establish document-specific or message-to-attachment grounding.

title: Bridging the Gap between Expression and Scene Text for Referring Expression Comprehension (Student Abstract)
abstract: Transfer-domain referring-expression work that incorporates scene text and associates textual content with corresponding visual regions before grounding a target expression. It is adjacent to screenshots and text-heavy attachments, but does not evaluate document rows, cells, or workplace messages.

title: Towards Unsupervised Referring Expression Comprehension with Visual Semantic Parsing
abstract: Transfer-domain work on grounding referring expressions in natural images using visual-semantic structure without fully supervised target-region labels. Its semantic parsing ideas may carry over to attachment grounding, but the evaluation domain is not documents.

title: RefDetector: A Simple Yet Effective Matching-based Method for Referring Expression Comprehension
abstract: Transfer-domain referring-expression comprehension using matching between language and candidate visual regions. It is relevant as a generic grounding mechanism but provides no validation for email language, document regions, tables, or cells.

title: KnowDR-REC: Auditing Knowledge-Conditioned Visual Grounding in Referring Expression Comprehension
abstract: Audits referring-expression grounding under knowledge-conditioned settings, including entity resolution, spatial grounding, and rejection of unsupported or hallucinated matches. This is transfer evidence for robust reference resolution, not direct workplace attachment evaluation.

title: Entity-Enhanced Adaptive Reconstruction Network for Weakly Supervised Referring Expression Grounding
abstract: Transfer-domain work on weakly supervised grounding of language expressions to visual entities and regions. It contributes visual-language alignment machinery but does not establish grounding into document-specific structural elements or revised attachments.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

title: Challenges in Information-Seeking QA: Unanswerable Questions and Paragraph Retrieval
abstract: Transfer-domain question-answering work that analyzes unanswerable questions together with evidence retrieval. It is relevant to distinguishing genuine evidence absence from successful evidence discovery, although it does not address multimodal document parsing failures or spatial provenance.

title: I Could've Asked That: Reformulating Unanswerable Questions
abstract: Studies document-grounded question answering when the original question is unanswerable and explores reformulating it into answerable alternatives. It offers transfer evidence for explicit handling of evidence absence, while parser failure and spatial grounding are outside its main scope.
